speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing; since infants cannot speak, I will rely on your observations to guide our exam. Can you tell me exactly what triggers these breathing difficulties, such as crying, feeding, or specific movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the worsening with neck flexion and vomiting suggests a structural issue rather than simple asthma. Can you describe the appearance of the larynx or any swelling in the neck when he is crying? REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of symptoms—stridor and wheezing worsening with neck flexion and feeding, but relieved by neck extension, along with post-feed vomiting—strongly suggests a vascular compression issue like a vascular ring or a large hemangioma. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound, Barium_Swallow. Have you noticed if the stridor changes pitch or severity when he turns his head to the left versus the right?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Born full term with no complications during birth. Social history: First child in the family. Lives with both parents. No exposure to smoking or pets in the household.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of significant past medical history and the specific triggers point toward a structural anomaly. Before I request the Barium Swallow images I mentioned, did you notice if he has trouble swallowing solids or if he coughs/chokes specifically when swallowing milk?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, diarrhea, rash, or other respiratory symptoms such as cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: No systemic symptoms like fever or rash are present. To further differentiate between a vascular ring and laryngeal cyst, I need to see the Barium Swallow results to rule out a structural obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Barium_Swallow

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Compression of the esophagus and trachea consistent with a vascular ring
